task: linux-hermit frontier: run a userspace program (busybox sh, hello world) inside the deterministic QEMU VM
milestone: L2 determinism (hermit run --strict --verify, bitwise-identical repeat) for a real userspace program executed inside a QEMU-Linux VM under Hermit
note_binary_vs_base: Test-only change (guest C + shell script); the hermit binary at 6044c2d3 is byte-identical in behavior to one built at 3056ae2 for this test. Branch rebased onto current main 3056ae2.
cpu_model_rationale: Host glibc targets x86-64-v2; its IFUNC resolvers use SSSE3/SSE4.1/SSE4.2 (pmaxud, palignr, pcmpistri). Default qemu64 advertises only up to SSE3 -> static glibc SIGILLs at exec. Enable exactly the x86-64-v2 set; nothing above it (no AVX/RDRAND) to avoid new nondeterminism sources.
guest_command: qemu-system-x86_64 -nodefaults -nic none -m 256M -accel tcg,thread=single -smp 1 -icount shift=0,sleep=off -rtc base=utc,clock=vm -cpu qemu64,+ssse3,+sse4.1,+sse4.2,+popcnt -kernel /boot/vmlinuz -initrd <run>/initramfs.cpio.gz -display none -serial stdio -monitor none -no-reboot -append 'console=ttyS0 panic=-1 rdinit=/init'
harness_verdict: All QEMU strict L2 userspace scenarios passed.
excluded_evidence: boot.stderr / verifier.stderr full --log info DETLOG dumps (tens of MB; >2 MiB; regenerate by rerun)
